Decide whether the single-turn study (Parrish et al., 2022b, 2204.05212v2), cited in the same marker, should get a parallel link

Note the setting difference: Parrish et al. set a limit of 5 minutes per judgment, from pilot response times, so that judges have adequate time to consider all the arguments and text snippets; Bowman et al. ask participants to answer under a 5-minute limit so that they cannot read the story in full and must rely on the model to gather relevant information
in.other_title: Bowman et al. use time-limited QuALITY, roughly paralleling Parrish et al.
in.rationale: Bowman et al. ask human participants to answer QuALITY questions under a 5-minute time limit, roughly paralleling Pang et al. (2022) and Parrish et al. (2022a,b), which prevents them from reading the story in full and forces them to rely on the model to gather relevant information. Parrish et al.'s two-turn study sets a limit of 5 minutes per judgment, from the pilot response times of its high-performing judges, so that judges have adequate time to consider all the arguments and text snippets. The passages show a parallel design choice made for different purposes, not Bowman et al. building on Parrish et al.'s judging protocol, and the target is a judging-protocol method that states no question or claim that Bowman et al. bear on; neither record bears on the other's claim, so the link proposes only SHARES_TOPIC for the shared 5-minute design choice.
in.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: 5-minute time limits for human participants on QuALITY questions; holds as a shared design choice only, since the limit is set per judgment of arguments in Parrish et al. and caps answering questions with model assistance in Bowman et al.

open_obligations: Note that time limit, judge pool and number of turns changed together.

out.other_title: Artificial time limit for judges; 60-120 s pilot variations made virtually no difference
out.rationale: Parrish et al. note their time limit makes the task more artificial than they would like and that 120 seconds might still be too short. The two-turn follow-up keeps the top 16 of 32 pilot judges and sets 5 minutes per judgment; judge selection and counter-arguments also changed, so time is not isolated.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a longer judging time changes the debate-argument null result, for human judges on 2-option QuALITY
